title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Madeira and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Madeira labels show the style, by sweetness or grape: Dry, Medium Dry, Medium Sweet, Sweet, or Sercial, Verdelho, Boal, Malvasia; and the age: 5, 10 or 15 Years Old, Colheita or Frasqueira. Canteiro may be noted. Tinta Negra can now be named. The IVBAM, the island's wine institute, certifies each bottle.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Sercial suits consommé, olives, almonds and sushi; Verdelho suits mushroom soups and pâté; Boal suits cheese, nuts and fruit cake; Malvasia suits chocolate, coffee desserts and Christmas pudding. Madeira is also a classic in cooking, like Madeira sauce for beef. Serve at 12 to 16 degrees, drier styles slightly cooler.
steps.highlight: Consommé with Sercial; chocolate with Malmsey

steps.prompt: Which Madeira suits dark chocolate desserts?

steps.body: An open bottle of Madeira keeps for months. It's the ideal wine to keep on hand for an occasional glass.

steps.prompt: Madeira must be finished within a day of opening.
steps.explanation: Not true. It's already oxidised, so it keeps for months.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show grape or sweetness, and age
Sercial suits soup; Malmsey suits chocolate
